title: 画龙点睛
subtitle: 最后两点最神奇
origin: 唐·张彦远《历代名画记·张僧繇》

moral.zh: 关键的一笔能让作品完整有神；动手前要看清哪里最重要。
moral.en: One essential finishing touch can bring a whole work to life; first understand what matters most.

idiomMeaning.zh: 给画好的龙点上眼睛；比喻在关键处加上一笔，使内容更加生动有力。
idiomMeaning.en: To dot the eyes of a painted dragon—adding the crucial finishing touch that makes something vivid and complete.

visualAnchor: Southern Dynasties Buddhist temple hall with cream plaster walls, dark wooden beams and warm daylight; painter Zhang Sengyou is a slender middle-aged man with an oval clean-shaven face, high scholar bun, deep-teal cross-collar robe, cream inner collar and rust-red sash; four large elegant ink-and-mineral-pigment dragon murals curl across two walls, initially all without painted pupils; fixed dark-wood brush, black inkstone and low painting table; dragons are majestic but friendly, with jade-green and muted-gold scales and no exposed fangs

pages.zh: 南朝画家张僧繇来到寺院，要在墙上画四条龙。
pages.en: The painter Zhang Sengyou came to a temple to paint four dragons on its walls.
pages.prompt: wide establishing hall scene, Zhang Sengyou sketching the first of four large wall dragons while assistants prepare pigments

pages.zh: 四条龙栩栩如生，却都没有点上眼睛。
pages.en: The four dragons looked wonderfully alive, but none had pupils in their eyes.
pages.prompt: visitors admiring all four finished dragon murals, each dragon eye visibly left without a dark pupil

pages.zh: 人们好奇地问：“为什么不给龙点上眼睛呢？”
pages.en: People asked, “Why have you not finished their eyes?”
pages.prompt: families asking the painter curiously while pointing gently toward the pupil-less dragon eyes

pages.zh: 张僧繇说：“眼睛一点，龙也许就会飞走。”
pages.en: Zhang Sengyou said, “Once I dot the eyes, the dragons may fly away.”
pages.prompt: painter holding his brush calmly and explaining as skeptical visitors smile, all four murals behind

pages.zh: 大家再三请求，他便提笔给其中两条龙点上眼睛。
pages.en: At their urging, he carefully dotted the eyes of two dragons.
pages.prompt: close storytelling scene, painter adding one small dark pupil to the second of exactly two selected dragons; other two remain pupil-less

pages.zh: 忽然云风涌动，两条点睛的龙从墙上腾空而起。
pages.en: Clouds stirred, and the two finished dragons lifted gently from the walls.
pages.prompt: exactly two completed friendly dragons rising from their murals into soft indoor clouds, visitors amazed but safe; two unfinished murals remain on the wall

pages.zh: 另外两条仍留在墙上。人们这才懂得什么叫画龙点睛。
pages.en: The other two stayed on the wall. Everyone understood the power of the finishing touch.
pages.prompt: turning point, visitors compare two empty mural spaces with the two remaining pupil-less dragons while painter watches thoughtfully

pages.zh: 张僧繇收好画笔：关键的一笔，要用在最重要的地方。
pages.en: Zhang put away his brush, knowing that the final touch belongs where it matters most.
pages.prompt: hopeful temple courtyard ending, painter cleaning his brush as two friendly dragons circle high in golden clouds

title: 曹冲称象
subtitle: 大船变成了秤

moral.zh: 大问题可以拆成容易处理的小步骤；认真观察，常能找到新办法。
moral.en: A big problem can be divided into manageable steps; careful observation often reveals a new solution.

idiomMeaning.zh: 曹冲利用船的浮沉和石头称出大象重量；常用来赞美善于观察、巧解难题。
idiomMeaning.en: Cao Chong weighed an elephant by using a boat's displacement and stones—a classic example of solving a hard problem with observation and ingenuity.

visualAnchor: Eastern Han riverside compound with wooden docks, tiled halls and a wide calm river; Cao Chong is a bright 7-year-old boy with round face, one neat child topknot, pale-gold short robe, dark-teal sash, brown trousers and black cloth shoes; Cao Cao is a broad middle-aged man with short moustache and beard, dark-red robe and black sash; fixed gentle gray Asian elephant with small rounded ears and no decorative armor; fixed wide flat-bottomed wooden barge with sturdy ramp, low rail and no sail; smooth gray weighing stones and wicker baskets

pages.zh: 有人送来一头大象，曹操和大家都想知道它有多重。
pages.en: A great elephant arrived, and Cao Cao wondered how much it weighed.
pages.prompt: wide establishing riverside courtyard, Cao Chong beside his father and the friendly elephant, officials gathered at a safe distance

pages.zh: 大象比牛还大，普通的秤根本放不下它。
pages.en: The elephant was far too large for any ordinary scale.
pages.prompt: officials comparing a small wooden balance scale with the enormous calm elephant, Cao Chong observing quietly

pages.zh: 曹冲望着河里的船，想起船会随着重量上下浮动。
pages.en: Watching a boat rise and sink, Cao Chong formed an idea.
pages.prompt: Cao Chong studying the fixed empty barge at the dock as gentle ripples touch its hull

pages.zh: 他让大象沿着宽木板，稳稳走上大船。
pages.en: He guided the elephant safely up a wide ramp and onto the barge.
pages.prompt: elephant walking calmly up the sturdy ramp onto the flat barge, adults guiding from the sides, no crowding

pages.zh: 船身下沉，曹冲在水面碰到船身的地方做了记号。
pages.en: The boat sank lower, and Cao Chong marked the waterline on its hull.
pages.prompt: side view of barge floating lower with elephant aboard, Cao Chong painting one simple horizontal waterline mark on the hull, no writing

pages.zh: 大象下船后，大家把石头装上船，直到水线重合。
pages.en: After the elephant stepped off, stones were loaded until the boat reached the same line.
pages.prompt: elephant safe on shore while adults load smooth stones into the barge until water meets the same single hull line

pages.zh: 再把石头分批称重相加，就完成了曹冲称象。
pages.en: They weighed the stones in batches and added them to find the elephant's weight.
pages.prompt: turning point, baskets of stones measured on a large balance scale while Cao Chong explains and the elephant watches nearby

pages.zh: 大家称赞曹冲：看懂规律，就能把大难题变成小步骤。
pages.en: Everyone praised Cao Chong for turning one huge problem into simple steps.
pages.prompt: warm closing dock scene, Cao Cao proudly rests a hand on Cao Chong's shoulder beside the relaxed elephant and barge

title: 老马识途
subtitle: 雾里带路的老伙伴

moral.zh: 经验是宝贵的本领；遇到陌生难题，也要尊重并善用有经验者的判断。
moral.en: Experience is a valuable skill; unfamiliar problems often become clearer when we respect knowledgeable guides.

idiomMeaning.zh: 老马认识走过的道路；比喻有经验的人熟悉情况，能够发挥引导作用。
idiomMeaning.en: An old horse knows the road—an experienced person can recognize the way and guide others.

visualAnchor: Ancient northern mountain route with pine forest, pale stone paths, layered ridges and soft morning mist; Guan Zhong is a calm lean middle-aged adviser with short beard, high scholar bun, navy traveling robe and rust-red cloak; Xi Peng is slightly older with graying temples, moss-green robe and beige cloak; fixed experienced gray mare has a white blaze, dark mane, gentle eyes and a simple brown cloth halter with no saddle armor; small peaceful traveling group carries packs but no weapons

pages.zh: 管仲和隰朋带着伙伴翻山回家，队伍里有一匹老灰马。
pages.en: Guan Zhong and Xi Peng traveled home through the mountains with an old gray mare.
pages.prompt: wide establishing mountain trail, both advisers walking beside the gray mare and a small peaceful pack group

pages.zh: 山雾越来越浓，弯弯的小路很快分不清方向。
pages.en: The mist thickened until every winding path looked the same.
pages.prompt: travelers paused safely at a misty three-way mountain fork, distant landmarks hidden

pages.zh: 大家看地图、找山峰，还是不知道哪条路通向家乡。
pages.en: Maps and mountain peaks offered no clear answer.
pages.prompt: Guan Zhong and Xi Peng study an unmarked route cloth while companions scan the foggy ridges

pages.zh: 管仲说：“老马走过这些路，也许它还记得回家的方向。”
pages.en: Guan Zhong said, “This old mare may remember the way home.”
pages.prompt: Guan Zhong gently loosening the mare's lead while Xi Peng and travelers watch with hope

pages.zh: 他们让老马走在前面，自己安静地跟在后面。
pages.en: They let the old mare lead and followed quietly behind.
pages.prompt: gray mare choosing one path with calm confidence, group following at a respectful distance

pages.zh: 老马沿着溪水、松树和熟悉的山口，一步步前进。
pages.en: She followed a stream, old pines, and a familiar mountain pass.
pages.prompt: mare leading beside a clear stream toward a recognizable pine-lined stone pass as mist begins to lift

pages.zh: 雾散以后，村庄出现在前方。大家赞叹老马识途。
pages.en: When the mist cleared, the village appeared. The old mare truly knew the road.
pages.prompt: turning point, sunlit village visible below as travelers smile and gently praise the mare

pages.zh: 他们给老马添好草料，也记住经验值得认真倾听。
pages.en: They fed and thanked their guide, remembering to listen to experience.
pages.prompt: hopeful village stable ending, advisers offer hay and water to the comfortable gray mare

title: 邯郸学步
subtitle: 找回自己的脚步

moral.zh: 学习别人可以借鉴长处，但不能盲目照搬，更不要丢掉适合自己的方式。
moral.en: Learn from others without copying blindly, and keep the way that genuinely fits you.

idiomMeaning.zh: 到邯郸模仿别人走路，反而忘了自己原来的步法；比喻机械模仿，连原有本领也丢掉。
idiomMeaning.en: Learning to walk in Handan but forgetting one's own gait—blind imitation that causes a person to lose their original ability.

visualAnchor: Warring States Handan city with broad stone street, gray-tiled shops, willow trees and warm spring light; the visitor from Yan is a slim 18-year-old youth with round clean-shaven face, high simple topknot, sky-blue short robe, navy sash, brown trousers and cloth shoes; recurring local walkers include a tall merchant in ochre, an elderly woman in plum-gray and a lively child in green; expressions are kind, never mocking

pages.zh: 燕国有个年轻人，听说邯郸人走路特别好看。
pages.en: A young man from Yan heard that the people of Handan walked beautifully.
pages.prompt: wide establishing city gate scene, Yan youth arriving and watching varied local pedestrians

pages.zh: 他站在街边观察，觉得每个人的步子都很有特点。
pages.en: He watched the street and admired every person's different stride.
pages.prompt: youth observing the tall merchant, elderly woman and child walking naturally along the broad street

pages.zh: 他先学高个商人的大步，又学孩子轻快的小步。
pages.en: First he copied a merchant's long stride, then a child's quick steps.
pages.prompt: youth awkwardly switching between exaggerated long and short steps, locals continuing kindly

pages.zh: 看见老人走得稳，他又立刻换成慢慢的小步。
pages.en: Seeing an elder's steady pace, he changed his walk again.
pages.prompt: youth imitating the elderly woman's small steady steps several paces behind her, respectful distance

pages.zh: 几种步子混在一起，他越走越别扭，差点绊住自己。
pages.en: All the copied steps tangled together until he nearly tripped.
pages.prompt: youth catching his balance safely with arms out, one foot crossed awkwardly, no fall or ridicule

pages.zh: 他坐下来想：每个人的身体和习惯本来就不一样。
pages.en: He sat and realized that every body and habit is different.
pages.prompt: youth resting on a stone bench, calmly observing the diverse walkers with new understanding

pages.zh: 盲目模仿会变成邯郸学步，连自己的步子也会忘记。
pages.en: Blind imitation had made him lose touch with his own natural walk.
pages.prompt: turning point, youth stands slowly and tests one relaxed natural step while locals encourage him

pages.zh: 他找回自己的节奏，也学会只借鉴真正适合的长处。
pages.en: He found his own rhythm and kept only the lessons that suited him.
pages.prompt: hopeful city-gate farewell, youth walking home naturally and confidently, no exaggerated gait

title: 程门立雪
subtitle: 雪中等候的一堂课

moral.zh: 认真求学需要尊重和耐心，也要用安全、体贴的方式照顾自己与他人。
moral.en: Learning asks for respect and patience, together with thoughtful care for ourselves and others.

idiomMeaning.zh: 学生冒雪在老师门外恭候；形容尊敬师长、诚心求学。
idiomMeaning.en: Students waiting respectfully in snow outside their teacher's door—a symbol of sincere learning and respect for teachers.

visualAnchor: Northern Song scholar Cheng Yi's quiet courtyard residence with gray tiles, wooden study door, covered eaves, bare plum tree and soft winter snow; Yang Shi is a calm 30-year-old scholar with oval clean-shaven face, high black bun, deep-teal padded robe and cream scarf; You Zuo is slightly stockier with short moustache, moss-green padded robe and rust scarf; Cheng Yi is an elderly teacher with gray beard, dark-brown robe and warm beige cloak; students wear dry cloaks and wait safely under the covered eaves, never shivering dangerously

pages.zh: 杨时和游酢带着疑问，来到程颐老师家中求教。
pages.en: Yang Shi and You Zuo came to Teacher Cheng Yi with an important question.
pages.prompt: wide establishing winter courtyard, the two students arrive with closed book bundles beneath light snow

pages.zh: 他们发现老师正在闭目休息，便没有敲门打扰。
pages.en: Finding their teacher resting, they chose not to disturb him.
pages.prompt: students quietly notice Cheng Yi resting inside through a partly open inner screen, then step back respectfully

pages.zh: 雪越下越密，两人披好斗篷，在屋檐下安静等候。
pages.en: As snow thickened, they wrapped their cloaks and waited beneath the eaves.
pages.prompt: both students warm and dry under covered eaves, snow collecting in open courtyard, calm patient expressions

pages.zh: 他们轻声整理问题，也互相提醒别着凉。
pages.en: They quietly organized their questions and made sure each other stayed warm.
pages.prompt: students speaking softly, one adjusts the other's scarf while holding closed book bundles

pages.zh: 程颐醒来开门，看见院中的积雪和耐心等候的学生。
pages.en: When Cheng Yi opened the door, he saw the snow and his patient students.
pages.prompt: elderly teacher opens the study door with surprised warmth, students bow from beneath the eaves

pages.zh: 他赶紧请两人进屋烤火、喝热茶，再慢慢解答问题。
pages.en: He welcomed them inside for warmth, tea, and a careful lesson.
pages.prompt: cozy study interior, teacher and students seated by a safe brazier with steaming tea, discussing an unmarked bamboo-slip bundle

pages.zh: 程门立雪，讲的是尊重老师、诚心求学的态度。
pages.en: Their snowy wait became a lasting symbol of respect and sincere learning.
pages.prompt: turning point, teacher answering as both students listen attentively beside the warm brazier

pages.zh: 老师也叮嘱：有诚意很好，安全照顾自己同样重要。
pages.en: The teacher added, “Sincerity matters, and so does taking good care of yourselves.”
pages.prompt: hopeful farewell at clearing sunset, teacher gives students warm hand covers before they leave

title: 韦编三绝
subtitle: 读断三次的书绳

moral.zh: 反复学习不是简单重复，而是在每一次阅读中多想一步、理解更深。
moral.en: Repeated study is not empty repetition; each return can bring a deeper question and clearer understanding.

idiomMeaning.zh: 编连竹简的皮绳多次断开；形容读书勤奋、反复钻研。
idiomMeaning.en: The leather cords binding bamboo slips broke repeatedly—a description of devoted reading and deep study.

visualAnchor: Late Spring and Autumn period study with wooden shelves, woven mat, low desk and warm oil lamp; Confucius is an elderly scholar with kind rectangular face, long neat gray beard, high dark-gray scholar bun, deep-brown robe, muted-teal sash and cream inner collar; fixed ancient book is a roll of narrow honey-brown bamboo slips joined by three dark leather cords, with only subtle abstract ink strokes and no legible characters; two young adult disciples in simple navy and moss robes

pages.zh: 孔子晚年仍然爱学习，常读一卷用皮绳编起的竹简。
pages.en: Even in later life, Confucius kept studying a book of bamboo slips.
pages.prompt: wide establishing study scene, Confucius unrolls the fixed three-cord bamboo-slip book as two disciples organize shelves

pages.zh: 清晨读，夜里也读，他每次都会停下来认真思考。
pages.en: He read at dawn and at night, pausing often to think.
pages.prompt: quiet dawn study, Confucius reading thoughtfully beside a fading oil lamp and cool window light

pages.zh: 竹简卷起又展开，连接它们的皮绳渐渐磨薄。
pages.en: The book rolled and unrolled until its leather cords wore thin.
pages.prompt: close storytelling view of Confucius's careful hands and visibly worn but intact leather cords

pages.zh: 一天，皮绳断了。弟子帮忙重新穿好，他继续读。
pages.en: One day a cord broke. A disciple rebound it, and the reading continued.
pages.prompt: one disciple gently threads a new leather cord through bamboo slips while Confucius watches appreciatively

pages.zh: 日子久了，新绳又断。这样的事一共发生了三次。
pages.en: With time, new cords wore out too—three times altogether.
pages.prompt: single continuous scene, three neatly coiled worn leather cords displayed beside the still-usable bamboo book, no montage panels

pages.zh: 孔子不只记住句子，还反复追问其中的道理。
pages.en: Confucius did more than remember words; he kept asking what they meant.
pages.prompt: teacher closes the bamboo book halfway and discusses an idea with two attentive disciples

pages.zh: 人们用韦编三绝，赞美他勤读又勤思的精神。
pages.en: People remembered the three broken bindings as a sign of devoted study.
pages.prompt: turning point, disciples hold the repaired bamboo book while Confucius reflects calmly

pages.zh: 读得多、想得深，旧书也能不断带来新的理解。
pages.en: Reading often and thinking deeply can make an old book feel new again.
pages.prompt: hopeful evening ending, Confucius teaches several students with the repaired bamboo book safely open on the desk

title: 水滴石穿
subtitle: 一枚铜钱和一块石头

moral.zh: 再小的行动只要不断累积，也会产生很大影响；好习惯和坏习惯都是如此。
moral.en: Small actions grow powerful through repetition, whether they form a good habit or a harmful one.

idiomMeaning.zh: 水滴长久落下能穿透石头；比喻力量虽小，只要坚持也能完成困难的事。
idiomMeaning.en: Constant drops can wear through stone—small but persistent effort can accomplish something difficult.

visualAnchor: Northern Song county office with pale stone courtyard, wooden treasury door, tiled eaves and one fixed rain chain dripping into a shallow hollow in a gray stone slab; Magistrate Zhang Guaiya is a composed middle-aged man with short moustache and beard, black official hat without writing, deep-navy robe and rust-red belt; the young clerk is slim with round clean-shaven face, low bun, pale-brown robe and teal sash; fixed single round bronze coin has a square center hole and no visible characters

pages.zh: 张乖崖管理县衙时，看见一位小吏从库房走出来。
pages.en: Magistrate Zhang Guaiya once saw a young clerk leaving the treasury.
pages.prompt: wide establishing county courtyard, magistrate notices the clerk near the wooden treasury door

pages.zh: 小吏手里藏着一枚铜钱，说：“只是一枚，没什么吧？”
pages.en: The clerk held one coin and said, “It is only one. Does it matter?”
pages.prompt: clerk opens his palm to reveal exactly one bronze coin, looking uncertain rather than defiant

pages.zh: 张乖崖没有责骂，带他去看屋檐下的一块石头。
pages.en: Instead of scolding him, Zhang led him to a stone beneath the eaves.
pages.prompt: magistrate calmly guides clerk toward the fixed rain chain and hollowed stone slab

pages.zh: 一滴水很轻，落在石头上，几乎看不出变化。
pages.en: One drop was tiny and seemed to change nothing.
pages.prompt: close view of one clear droplet landing on the gray stone hollow as both men observe

pages.zh: 可年年滴、天天滴，坚硬的石头也被滴出了小坑。
pages.en: But years of drops had slowly made a hollow in the hard stone.
pages.prompt: magistrate points to the smooth shallow hollow formed by many drops, clerk studies it closely

pages.zh: 张乖崖说：“小事不断累积，也会变成很大的结果。”
pages.en: “Small actions add up,” Zhang explained. “They can become a great result.”
pages.prompt: magistrate speaks kindly beside dripping eave, clerk compares the single coin with the stone hollow

pages.zh: 小吏明白水滴石穿的道理，马上把铜钱放回库房。
pages.en: Understanding the lesson, the clerk returned the coin at once.
pages.prompt: turning point, clerk places the single coin back into an open wooden cash box while magistrate watches

pages.zh: 从此他认真记好每一笔，也让诚实成为每天的习惯。
pages.en: From then on, he kept careful accounts and practiced honesty every day.
pages.prompt: hopeful treasury ending, clerk counts coins into tidy trays with magistrate approving nearby, no visible writing

title: 熟能生巧
subtitle: 铜钱孔里的油线
origin: 宋·欧阳修《归田录·卖油翁》

moral.zh: 稳定练习会让动作越来越熟练；有本领也要保持谦虚，继续学习。
moral.en: Steady practice makes skill feel natural, and true ability grows best alongside humility.

idiomMeaning.zh: 熟练以后就能找到巧妙方法；说明反复实践可以提高技能。
idiomMeaning.en: Practice breeds skill—repeated experience leads to fluency and clever technique.

visualAnchor: Northern Song country practice yard with willow tree, low wall and warm afternoon light; Chen Yaozi is a confident athletic 35-year-old man with straight brows, high topknot, dark-teal short robe, rust sash and leather wrist guard; fixed bow is unstrung except during target practice, arrows have blunt dark tips and are aimed only at a round straw target far from all people; elderly oil seller has silver low bun, short gray beard, ochre-brown robe, navy sash and two wooden oil gourds; fixed round bronze coin with square hole and no writing sits over one gourd mouth; oil is golden and clean

pages.zh: 陈尧咨擅长射箭，常常正中远处的草靶。
pages.en: Chen Yaozi was an excellent archer who often hit the distant straw target.
pages.prompt: wide establishing yard, Chen releases one blunt arrow toward the isolated straw target while everyone stands safely behind him

pages.zh: 大家连声称赞，卖油翁却只在旁边微微点头。
pages.en: The crowd praised him, while an old oil seller simply nodded.
pages.prompt: Chen stands with bow safely lowered as neighbors applaud and the elderly seller watches calmly beside oil gourds

pages.zh: 陈尧咨问：“你也懂射箭吗？”老人说：“只是练得熟。”
pages.en: Chen asked, “Do you know archery?” The elder replied, “You have practiced well.”
pages.prompt: friendly conversation, Chen's bow unstrung and resting on a rack, seller gestures modestly

pages.zh: 老人把一枚铜钱放在油葫芦口，露出中间的小孔。
pages.en: The seller placed a coin over a gourd, leaving its tiny center hole open.
pages.prompt: close scene of seller safely placing the fixed square-hole coin flat over the oil gourd mouth

pages.zh: 他舀起一勺油，细细的油线穿过小孔，铜钱一点没湿。
pages.en: A thin stream of oil passed through the hole without wetting the coin.
pages.prompt: golden oil forms one precise thin stream through the square coin hole into the gourd, Chen watches in amazement

pages.zh: 卖油翁笑着说：“没有神奇，只是这双手做得多了。”
pages.en: The seller smiled. “It is no magic. My hands have done this many times.”
pages.prompt: seller sets ladle down and shows relaxed steady hands, Chen looks thoughtful and respectful

pages.zh: 陈尧咨明白了：反复练习，才能熟能生巧。
pages.en: Chen understood that repeated practice creates skill.
pages.prompt: turning point, Chen bows slightly in thanks while the seller holds the dry coin beside the gourd

pages.zh: 他不再骄傲，继续认真练习，也更懂得尊重别人的本领。
pages.en: He returned to practice with humility and greater respect for others' skills.
pages.prompt: hopeful sunset ending, Chen practices calm stance with no arrow nocked while seller walks past smiling

title: 望梅止渴
subtitle: 山坡后的酸梅林
origin: 南朝宋·刘义庆《世说新语·假谲》

moral.zh: 想象和鼓励能帮助我们暂时坚持，但真正的需要仍要用实际办法解决。
moral.en: Imagination and encouragement can help us persist for a while, but real needs still require practical solutions.

idiomMeaning.zh: 想到酸梅就分泌口水、暂时缓解口渴；比喻用想象安慰自己或别人。
idiomMeaning.en: Thinking of sour plums to ease thirst—using imagination to provide temporary comfort when the real thing is unavailable.

visualAnchor: Late Eastern Han summer countryside with dry golden road, low green hills, sparse shade trees and shimmering warm air; Cao Cao is a broad middle-aged leader with short moustache and beard, black traveling cap, deep-red lightweight robe and dark-teal belt; small peaceful traveling group wears tan, moss and navy robes, carries cloth packs and empty water gourds, with no armor or weapons; imagined plum grove has leafy trees full of small green plums and must appear only as a soft dreamlike visualization until the group reaches a real clear stream

pages.zh: 夏日里，曹操带着一队人赶路，水壶很快都空了。
pages.en: On a hot summer journey, Cao Cao's group soon ran out of water.
pages.prompt: wide establishing dry road, Cao Cao and peaceful travelers check empty gourds beneath strong sun

pages.zh: 太阳火辣辣，大家口干舌燥，脚步也越来越慢。
pages.en: The fierce sun made everyone thirsty and slow.
pages.prompt: travelers rest briefly in a small patch of shade, tired but safe, Cao Cao studying the hills

pages.zh: 曹操想起青梅又酸又多汁，心里有了一个办法。
pages.en: Cao Cao remembered juicy sour green plums and formed an idea.
pages.prompt: close thoughtful scene, Cao Cao imagines a small soft-edged vision of green plums, clearly not a real nearby grove

pages.zh: 他指着前方说：“翻过山坡，就有一大片梅林！”
pages.en: He pointed ahead. “Beyond that hill lies a grove of plums!”
pages.prompt: Cao Cao points toward the next hill as travelers look up with renewed attention, no actual plum trees visible

pages.zh: 大家想到酸梅，嘴里生出津液，又有力气继续走了。
pages.en: Thinking of sour plums made their mouths water and helped them keep moving.
pages.prompt: travelers walk toward the hill with brighter expressions; a faint dreamlike plum image floats only as imagination

pages.zh: 越过山坡，他们终于找到一条清清的小溪。
pages.en: Beyond the hill, they finally found a clear stream.
pages.prompt: group discovers a real shaded stream, kneeling safely to fill gourds; no plum grove present

pages.zh: 这就是望梅止渴：想象能暂时鼓劲，却不能代替真正的水。
pages.en: That was relief through imagined plums—useful for a moment, but no substitute for water.
pages.prompt: turning point, Cao Cao explains beside the stream while travelers drink and understand

pages.zh: 休息以后，他们装满水壶，也学会下次提前做好准备。
pages.en: After resting, they filled every gourd and planned better for the next journey.
pages.prompt: hopeful ending, group departs along a greener road with visibly full water gourds

title: 孟母三迁
subtitle: 为成长寻找好邻居
origin: 西汉·刘向《列女传·母仪传》

moral.zh: 环境会影响习惯，家人的引导也很重要；真正成长还需要自己的认真努力。
moral.en: Our surroundings shape habits, and family guidance matters; lasting growth also needs our own effort.

idiomMeaning.zh: 孟子的母亲为选择合适的成长环境多次搬家；形容重视环境对教育的影响。
idiomMeaning.en: Mencius's mother moved repeatedly to find a better environment for her child—a symbol of thoughtful guidance and the influence of surroundings.

visualAnchor: Warring States Zou region with three recurring neighborhoods: a quiet respectful memorial field with simple stone markers and no graves opened, a lively covered market, and a calm village school courtyard; young Mencius is a curious 6-year-old boy with round face, one small topknot, pale-blue short robe, beige sash and brown trousers; his mother is a warm composed woman with oval face, black hair in a low bun, plum-red cross-collar robe, dark-teal sash and cream shawl; fixed household belongings fit in two wicker baskets and one rolled sleeping mat

pages.zh: 孟子小时候和母亲住在一片安静的祭礼场所附近。
pages.en: When Mencius was small, he and his mother lived near a place of memorial ceremonies.
pages.prompt: wide establishing respectful memorial field, mother and child carry water near simple stone markers, no sadness or scary elements

pages.zh: 他常模仿大人的祭礼动作，孟母觉得这里不适合久住。
pages.en: He often copied the ceremonies, and his mother decided the place was not right for them.
pages.prompt: young Mencius imitates a formal bow with innocent curiosity as mother watches thoughtfully

pages.zh: 他们搬到集市旁，孟子又学着商贩高声叫卖、讨价还价。
pages.en: They moved beside a market, where Mencius began copying the loud vendors.
pages.prompt: same mother and child beside their wicker baskets in lively market, Mencius playfully imitates a vendor with empty hands

pages.zh: 孟母想了想，带着他再次搬家，来到一所学堂附近。
pages.en: His mother moved once more, this time near a school.
pages.prompt: mother and child walk with two baskets and rolled mat toward a peaceful school courtyard

pages.zh: 学堂里，孩子们有礼地读书、提问，也互相帮助。
pages.en: At the school, children read, asked questions, and helped one another.
pages.prompt: Mencius watches diverse pupils learning cooperatively through the open school gate, no visible writing

pages.zh: 孟子受到吸引，坐进课堂，开始认真听老师讲课。
pages.en: Drawn to the lessons, Mencius joined the class and listened carefully.
pages.prompt: same boy seated among pupils before a kind teacher, mother watches quietly from the doorway

pages.zh: 孟母三迁，是母亲用心选择环境，也耐心陪伴孩子成长。
pages.en: The three moves showed a mother's thoughtful care in shaping her child's surroundings.
pages.prompt: turning point, mother and child walk home from school together, discussing the day warmly

pages.zh: 孟子也明白：好环境带来机会，真正学会还要靠自己努力。
pages.en: Mencius learned that a good environment offers opportunity, while effort makes learning his own.
pages.prompt: hopeful home ending, Mencius reviews an unmarked bamboo-slip bundle while mother mends cloth nearby
